name: The Goode Life
text: [overview] Seasonal snow may need crampons or an axe later in the year.
[approach] Cross the moraine boulder fields to the second buttress left of the main buttress and go over a snowfield to the base.
[approach] Late in the season, ice may call for boots, crampons or an axe.

name: Avalanche Gulch
text: [overview] The standard and most-climbed route on Mount Shasta, a long snow climb gaining about 7,000 vertical feet from Bunny Flat to the 14,179 ft summit.
[overview] It is non-technical but steep and demanding, and needs an ice axe, crampons, a helmet and solid self-arrest skills.
[beta] From Helen Lake, climb straight up Avalanche Gulch on snow, heading between the dark rock of The Heart on the left and Thumb Rock on the right.
[beta] Most parties climb one of the steep snow or ice chutes that cut through the Red Banks;
[hazards] Steep snow and ice.
[obj_haz] Hard, icy snow in the morning where a slip can turn into a long slide.
[watch_out] Glissading with crampons on
[gear] Ice axe.
[gear] Crampons.
[detailed_rack] Gear needs run from none up through snow-climbing equipment and beyond, varying with the season and circumstances.
[what_to_bring] Glacier glasses and high-SPF sunscreen.
[what_to_bring] Extra layer or durable pants for glissading.
[what_to_bring] Stove and fuel for melting snow.
[what_to_bring] Ice axe.

name: Hotlum-Wintun Ridge
text: [overview] from there climb straight up between the two glaciers, Hotlum and Wintun.
[overview] Above 11,000' it steepens and two snowfields, each close to 45 degrees, flank a rocky tongue.
[overview] Most parties traverse climber's left onto the Wintun Glacier above;
[detailed_rack] Snow climbing gear at a basic level, and skis or a snowboard are strongly advised.
[approach] The trail is faint and disappears under snow, so head up toward the summit, which stays in view, along the open slopes south of the Brewer Creek drainage.
[approach] The route climbs the broad snowfield above the camp between the Hotlum and Wintun glaciers, so recognise the start by the large snowfield rising straight above the bench.

[descent_text] From the summit, angle down the steep upper chute and onto the Wintun side, where the slope is steepest and a fall can slide a long way, so keep the axe in hand and do not glissade carelessly.
[descent_text] Cross back over the rib to the snowfield between the glaciers, below the high traverse, then run down the snowfield to the bench camp and the Brewer Creek drainage to the trailhead.
[descent_text] The route has no major crevasses or fumaroles, but the snow can turn to heavy slush in the afternoon.

[overview] Conditions range between steep neve over ice and bulletproof blue ice.
[detailed_rack] Early season may call for pickets or some rock gear;
[approach] Turn left and head south to the foot of the North Peak snowfield, and climb it to the couloir.
